events.summary:
H1 is the best-supported hypothesis and clearly outranks H2-H4 on temporal order, scope, and mechanism: a leak-like monotonic memory climb begins 2026-03-21 ~01:00-02:00Z, immediately after dep-5402 (notification-service v3.8.0, "Add in-memory template cache") and ~45h before the Kafka retention change; consumer lag spikes coincide with, rather than precede, the restarts; all three restarts are exit-137 with a clean sawtooth; and no other deployment/config change exists in the window. H2 is directly contradicted (two of three OOMs predate cfg-2410), H3 is only negatively supported (notification-service get_config_changes = 0; no infra change found), and H4 has no evidence of a producer-side change.

However, H1's final hop — "unbounded key space => heap grows until OOM" — is still an assumption, not a verified finding. The deployment description ("add in-memory template cache") came from a deployment record, not from cache configuration or heap profiling, and F9-F11 are all memory_pct/restart-counter aggregates. Two things could change or hollow out the ranking: (a) if the TemplateCache is actually bounded (max-size/TTL), H1's mechanism collapses and the leak must lie elsewhere in v3.8.0 or outside the deploy, and (b) if the container memory limit was recently raised/lowered or the node was under contention, the "genuine heap growth to 94% of limit" reading is confounded. Neither is answered by current data; both are cheaply obtainable. Also note the analysis rests on a single metric family (memory_pct from one source) for the core mechanism, and the dependency side still has two unexecuted calls (2026-03-23 deployments; settlement-service map) plus no evidence of what the "Kafka maintenance" actually did — relevant to whether the shared broker is an amplifying factor even if not the origin.

Confidence cap 0.72 is defensible as an upper bound but should not rise until the unbounded-cache claim is verified against the actual cache implementation/config and a second, independent memory signal.

The shared-side silence test I requested was run: settlement-service (co-consumer) and both producers are flat in memory, restarts and error_rate across 03-20..03-24 with no change at 18:00Z [F19,F20,F21,F24]. H4's premise (producer-side anomaly) is directly negated for memory/error; H3 is negatively supported by zero recorded config changes for notification-service in 2026-03-01..03-23 [F34] and by the clean leak-like climb [F26,F27,F30]. No deployment at all occurred on 03-23 [F33].

CAVEATS CAP.CODE. Two residual weaknesses keep this below 0.85: (1) the unbounded-cache mechanism is supported by an ABSENCE — no eviction field in a two-line change summary — plus the entry-count logs, not by code inspection; boundedness is inferred, not read [F31, T4]; (2) memory_pct is the only memory gauge for this service (heap_used_bytes not_found, available_metrics has no RSS/heap series) [F25], so the leak claim rests on one metric family plus cache-entry logs. A secondary, correctly-assumed detail: the live container memory request/limit was never retrievable by any tool, and no broker-side metric exists, so the "growth to the limit" reading and the breadth of the Kafka maintenance window (retention-only per the record) remain assumptions. None of these can flip the ranking — they would only soften or sharpen a mechanism whose onset, scope, sawtooth periodicity and neighbour-isolation all agree — so I cap at 0.78 and accept rather than spend the remaining budget.

Residual uncertainty should be recorded as explicit assumptions: (a) boundedness inferred from the absence of an eviction policy in the record, not from a diff; (b) memory_pct tracks container working set dominated by the TemplateCache heap; (c) cfg-2410 was retention-only with no broker reassignment.

critiques.summary:
H1 is the best-supported hypothesis and clearly outranks H2-H4 on temporal order, scope, and mechanism: a leak-like monotonic memory climb begins 2026-03-21 ~01:00-02:00Z, immediately after dep-5402 (notification-service v3.8.0, "Add in-memory template cache") and ~45h before the Kafka retention change; consumer lag spikes coincide with, rather than precede, the restarts; all three restarts are exit-137 with a clean sawtooth; and no other deployment/config change exists in the window. H2 is directly contradicted (two of three OOMs predate cfg-2410), H3 is only negatively supported (notification-service get_config_changes = 0; no infra change found), and H4 has no evidence of a producer-side change.

However, H1's final hop — "unbounded key space => heap grows until OOM" — is still an assumption, not a verified finding. The deployment description ("add in-memory template cache") came from a deployment record, not from cache configuration or heap profiling, and F9-F11 are all memory_pct/restart-counter aggregates. Two things could change or hollow out the ranking: (a) if the TemplateCache is actually bounded (max-size/TTL), H1's mechanism collapses and the leak must lie elsewhere in v3.8.0 or outside the deploy, and (b) if the container memory limit was recently raised/lowered or the node was under contention, the "genuine heap growth to 94% of limit" reading is confounded. Neither is answered by current data; both are cheaply obtainable. Also note the analysis rests on a single metric family (memory_pct from one source) for the core mechanism, and the dependency side still has two unexecuted calls (2026-03-23 deployments; settlement-service map) plus no evidence of what the "Kafka maintenance" actually did — relevant to whether the shared broker is an amplifying factor even if not the origin.

Confidence cap 0.72 is defensible as an upper bound but should not rise until the unbounded-cache claim is verified against the actual cache implementation/config and a second, independent memory signal.

challenges.issue: The central mechanism hop — 'TemplateCache key space is effectively unbounded' — is an ASSUMPTION sourced from the deployment message text, not verified from code/config (no max-size, TTL, eviction, or heap-profile evidence). If the cache is actually bounded, the leak is unlocated and H1's causal chain breaks, which could re-rank the hypotheses.

Memory onset precedence is chronologically tight but not causally verified: the climb begins 03-21T01:00-02:00Z while the deploy is stamped 03-21T00:00:00Z, and the underlying series is 2-hour buckets, so 'immediately after the deploy' rests on bucket granularity. Deploy timestamp precision vs. climb onset should be confirmed.

Memory evidence is a single metric (memory_pct) from one query source; 'healthy/leak-like' is not corroborated by an independent signal (RSS/working set, GC/heap from JVM metrics, or container-level memory). A single-metric basis for the core mechanism is a data-quality gap.

The post-restart residual (~46-48%) and ~94% 'limit' peaks are assumed to correspond to the configured container memory limit; the actual requests/limits values were never retrieved (get_config_changes returned 0, which answers only 'no change recorded', not the current value). H3's alternative (limit lowered / node contention) is therefore dismissed on absence-of-record rather than on the limit value.

Correctly ranked low and contradicted (2 of 3 OOMs precede cfg-2410), but the Kafka maintenance scope was never established beyond the single retention config line — no broker restart/reassignment event. This does not change the origin ranking but leaves the shared-broker amplification path untested.

Dismissed on a negative config-change query for notification-service only; no node-level data (node memory pressure, co-tenant pods on the host, actual container limits) was retrieved. Contradiction rests on inference from F9/F10 rather than direct node evidence.

Dismissed without testing the producer side at all (no order-service/payment-service message-rate, size, or memory data). 'No producer-side change recorded' rules out a deploy but not workload-driven volume/size anomalies, which is exactly the untested path.

critiques.summary:
H1 remains clearly the best-supported origin, and the round-2 work closed the two specific blockers I named in round 1 without opening a new ranking-level gap.

GROUNDING / TEMPORAL ORDER. The causal chain now rests on verified observations at every hop that decides origin: dep-5402 deployed notification-service v3.8.0 adding a ConcurrentHashMap TemplateCache on the render path and was never rolled back [F1,F2]; the change record contains no max-size/TTL/eviction field and the key schema (template+locale+userSegment) is uncapped by anything in evidence [F31,F32]; TemplateCache stats logs show strictly linear entry growth with evictions=0, ~51,750-54,000 entries per interval, resetting exactly at each restart with near-identical trajectories across all three cycles [F28]; memory_pct is verifiably flat 03-20T00:00Z->03-21T01:00Z then begins a monotonic climb at 03-21T01:00-02:00Z [F9,F26]; the sawtooth resets to ~46-47% and refills along the same slope across 03-21, 03-22 and 03-23 [F7,F8,F10,F27,F30]. Onset (03-21 ~01:00Z) sits immediately after the only relevant change and ~45h before cfg-2410.

SCOPE / ALTERNATIVES. H2 is now contradicted on three independent axes rather than dismissed: two of three OOMs predate cfg-2410 [F18]; notification-service consumer lag is flat inside the cfg-2410 window (17:00Z-19:20Z, max <=93) and spikes only in the 19:40Z bucket, at/after the 19:59:21Z restart [F22,F23]; and cfg-2410 touched exactly one key on one service with no consumer-group, partition, replica or message-size setting [F35]. The shared-side silence test I requested was run: settlement-service (co-consumer) and both producers are flat in memory, restarts and error_rate across 03-20..03-24 with no change at 18:00Z [F19,F20,F21,F24]. H4's premise (producer-side anomaly) is directly negated for memory/error; H3 is negatively supported by zero recorded config changes for notification-service in 2026-03-01..03-23 [F34] and by the clean leak-like climb [F26,F27,F30]. No deployment at all occurred on 03-23 [F33].

CAVEATS CAP.CODE. Two residual weaknesses keep this below 0.85: (1) the unbounded-cache mechanism is supported by an ABSENCE — no eviction field in a two-line change summary — plus the entry-count logs, not by code inspection; boundedness is inferred, not read [F31, T4]; (2) memory_pct is the only memory gauge for this service (heap_used_bytes not_found, available_metrics has no RSS/heap series) [F25], so the leak claim rests on one metric family plus cache-entry logs. A secondary, correctly-assumed detail: the live container memory request/limit was never retrievable by any tool, and no broker-side metric exists, so the "growth to the limit" reading and the breadth of the Kafka maintenance window (retention-only per the record) remain assumptions. None of these can flip the ranking — they would only soften or sharpen a mechanism whose onset, scope, sawtooth periodicity and neighbour-isolation all agree — so I cap at 0.78 and accept rather than spend the remaining budget.

Residual uncertainty should be recorded as explicit assumptions: (a) boundedness inferred from the absence of an eviction policy in the record, not from a diff; (b) memory_pct tracks container working set dominated by the TemplateCache heap; (c) cfg-2410 was retention-only with no broker reassignment.

challenges.issue: The mechanism's decisive link (cache is unbounded) is inferred from the ABSENCE of a max-size/TTL/eviction field in a two-line change summary [F31] plus entry-count logs [F28]; no commit, diff or cache config was retrievable, so boundedness is not positively verified. This is the last unverified hop in an otherwise evidence-backed chain.

The core memory claim rests on a single metric family: memory_pct is the only memory signal for notification-service (heap_used_bytes returned not_found; available_metrics lacks RSS/heap) [F25]. Corroboration comes from cache-entry logs, which are service-emitted rather than independent.

Container memory request/limit was never retrievable by any tool, so 'growth to ~96% of the limit' and '~46% residual' are interpreted relative to an unverified limit; combined with no node-level memory evidence, H3 is excluded by record-absence [F34] and the leak-like shape, not by live spec.

H2's scope mechanism is asserted by the reporter and not directly contradicted on the broker side because no broker metric or reassignment event exists; it is contradicted indirectly via neighbour silence [F19,F20,F21,F24] and the lag-vs-cfg-2410 ordering [F22,F23]. This is adequate for ranking but not a positive refutation of the broker-side claim.
